title: Crookes tube jump observed by Brown as a student

tellings.quote: And what he observed was that when a high voltage was applied to the Crookes tube, he noticed that the wire conducting the voltage jumped.

plain: In the 1920s, as a student at Caltech, the inventor Townsend Brown is said to have noticed that when he put a high voltage across a Crookes tube, a glass vacuum tube that glows under electricity, the wire carrying the voltage "jumped". The journalist Nick Cook tells this to Michels in a documentary about Brown, as the moment that started Brown's later work on using electricity to make things move, which Cook links to craft like UFOs.
